title.narrative: Kyatune Sustainable Livelihoods and Disaster Risk Reduction Project

description.narrative:
The Kyatune Sustainable Livelihoods and Disaster Risk Reduction Project is a pilot phase intended to serve the community living in Kyatune Location in Kitui District. The project targets 2,000 most poor and vulnerable drought-prone individuals in the location.
The overarching goal of the proposed project is ‘to improve resilience of most poor vulnerable drought-prone communities of Kyatune through creation of economic community based assets to mitigate the effects of drought and climate change’
The project aims at achieving four major closely interrelated outcomes. Firstly; improved capacity for the local communities residing in Kyatune to prepare and mitigate against the effects of droughts and other natural calamities by 2012 through training local leaders on DRR, drought contingency planning, awareness creation on DRR and climate change, formation of Early Warning Groups and preparation and dissemination of early warning information, establishment of tree nurseries and planting of ecologically friendly trees. Secondly, Increased availability, access and management of water for domestic, agricultural and livestock production through out the dry season by 2012 through construction and protection of water structures through voucher for work system, formation and training of Water User Associations on water management and DRR, awareness creation on hygiene and sanitation and construction of ar-baloo toilet slabs for the most poor and vulnerable households. Thirdly; increased food production through better farming technologies such as community demonstration farms, green houses at household level, drip/watering irrigation instead of relying on rain-fed agriculture, support for horticultural crops, vegetable and fruit tree growing, preparation and application of compost manure, training on conservation agriculture, establishment of producer marketing groups, awareness creation on drought tolerant crops and establishment of seed banks. Finally; the project also aims at achieving increased household incomes through improved market access for sale of farm produce. This outcome will be achieved through supporting most affected households with ghalla goats and bucks, training Community Animal Health Assistants (paravets) on animal husbandry, increasing farmers’ access to market information through establishment of market information centres and boards and supporting farmers to establish market linkages. Further, energy saving technologies will be incorporated in the training sessions.
The project will utilize the existing Diocesan Church structures especially the Parishes to reach out to the intended beneficiaries. The project will also collect and analyze gender-specific information on the participation of women and other vulnerable groups. The project will take into consideration the interests of women, children, youth and poor men as well as the voices of the community leaders and other individuals and community based groups in ensuring that human rights upheld.
